text.p: These are the main stories in Latvian newspapers on Wednesday. Prepared for Reuters by the Co-operation Fund. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy:

- Latvian President Guntis Ulmanis is on visit to Turkey. Meeting with Turkish president Suleiman Demirel, he announced that Latvia expects Turkey to support its efforts in joining NATO. The foreign ministers of the two countries signed agreements on promotion and protection of investments and on trade and co-operation. Ulmanis has also met the Turkish Prime Minister, Netzmetdin Erbakan.

- A Latvian parliament delegation in Moscow met the deputy mayor of Moscow, Oleg Tolkachev. The mayor, Jury Lushkov, was said to be on a business trip outside Moscow. The vice-mayor said the major obstacles in relations between Latvia and Moscow is the situation of ethnic Russians in Latvia, as well as some laws which have been adopted by local governments.
- The three commanders of the Baltic states navies have drafted a plan of military co-operation, which includes six or seven joint military exercises, including those in co-operation with NATO.
- Latvian foreign policy experts are sceptical about the concept of a trilateral Latvian-Russian-NATO treaty, proposed by Russian Duma deputy speaker, Alexander Shokhin.

- The head of the Latvian parliament human rights committee, Anton Seiksts, denied accusations by Russia side that Latvia is too slow in naturalising non-citizens. Of almost 33,000 non-citizens entitled to naturalisation in 1996, only 560 have applied for citizenship.
- The finance ministry will pay off the debts owed to energy producers by local governments and industrial enterprises.

- The president of leading bank Parex Bank, Valery Kargin, told journalists in Moscow that the Latvian bank is going to invest in Russia's oil industry, transport and communications as well as give credits to Russia's local governments.
